extraction.name: EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Leaming Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification
extraction.description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting out of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images. The dataset is multi-spectral, georeferenced, and based on openly and freely accessible Earth observation data.
extraction.license: The underlying Sentinel-2 satellite images are openly and freely accessible and can be used for any application (commercial or non-commercial use). The EuroSAT dataset is made publicly available.
extraction.creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
extraction.publisher: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (IGARSS), 2018
extraction.citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. Introducing EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Leaming Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification In Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (IGARSS), 2018 IEEE Intemational . IEEE, 2018.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Satellite images of European cities distributed in over 34 countries were gathered. The dataset consists of 27,000 georeferenced and labeled image patches, measuring 64x64 pixels, with 10 different land use and land cover classes. Images were extracted all over the year to capture high intra-class variance.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral image data provided by the Sentinel-2A satellite, openly and freely accessible through the Earth observation program Copernicus, downloaded via Amazon S3. Images were chosen from cities covered in the European Urban Atlas.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The Sentinel-2A satellite was launched in June 2015 and Sentinel-2B in March 2017. The satellites capture data about every five days and are expected to operate for 20-30 years.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Bands with a lower spatial resolution (60m or 20m) were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation for single-band image evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Satellite images with a low cloud level were selected. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction; images with color cast were intentionally not filtered to advocate the classifier to learn these cases. Bad image patches (e.g., mislabeled, full of snow or ice) were sorted out during manual checking.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The 27,000 image patches were manually checked multiple times, and the ground truth was corrected by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. The 10 land use and land cover classes were chosen based on their visibility at 10 meters per pixel resolution and frequent coverage by the European Urban Atlas. The composition of classes and their relationships are specified in the mapping guide of the European Urban Atlas [40].
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Manual checking involved correcting ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is based on Sentinel-2 satellite images, which are part of an open and free Earth observation program whose satellites deliver images for the next 20-30 years, allowing continuous monitoring. The EuroSAT dataset itself is a static release made publicly available.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The classification system can be used for detecting deforestation, which is a main contributor to climate change, and thus assists in noticing illegal clearing of forests. This has implications for urban area development, nature protection, and sustainable development.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. The patch-based classification system does not allow a finely graduated per-pixel segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of deep neural networks for land use and land cover classification. Specific applications include detecting land use and land cover changes, assisting in improving geographical maps (e.g., OpenStreetMap), monitoring land surfaces, and applications in agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, or environmental monitoring.
